parsed.summary: The first theorem formalizes Theorem 1.2. Some finite graph H on Fin q is connected, bipartite and 2-degenerate, and has constants c, ε > 0 with c·n^{3/2+ε} ≤ ex(n,H) for all sufficiently large n. It adds a side condition: in every proper 2-coloring, each color class contains a vertex of degree > 2. The second theorem is the negation of Erdős's degeneracy conjecture ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}), stated faithfully for all r > 0. The main caveat is coverage: Theorem 1.1 (failure of compactness) is not formalized.

glossary.plain: N_G(v) ∩ s: the neighbors of v lying in the finite set s.
Every nonempty finite vertex set s contains a vertex with at most r neighbors in s, i.e. every nonempty induced subgraph has a vertex of degree ≤ r.
glossary.note: Restricting to induced subgraphs is equivalent to quantifying over all subgraphs. Since all graphs here are finite, quantifying over Finsets is complete.

glossary.plain: For all r > 0 and every finite bipartite r-degenerate graph H (on Fin q), ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}) as n → ∞.
glossary.note: The exponent is computed in ℝ with r cast to ℝ, so there is no truncation issue. Excluding r = 0 is harmless.

lean_claims.plain: There exist q and a graph H on Fin q such that all of the following hold: (a) H is connected, bipartite and 2-degenerate; (b) for every proper 2-coloring and each color side, the maximum degree over that side exceeds 2, which forces both sides to be nonempty; (c) there exist c > 0 and ε > 0 with c·n^{3/2+ε} ≤ ex(n,H) for all sufficiently large n.
There exist r > 0 and a finite bipartite r-degenerate graph H such that ex(n,H) is not O(n^{2−1/r}).

paper_claims.plain: There is a finite nonempty family F of connected bipartite graphs, each containing a cycle, with ex(n,F) = O(n^{4/3−1/48}) while ex(n,F) = Ω(n^{4/3}) for each F ∈ F.
There exist a connected bipartite 2-degenerate H and c, ε > 0 with ex(n,H) ≥ c n^{3/2+ε} for all sufficiently large n.
Not every bipartite r-degenerate H has ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}).

coverage.why: Same conclusion, plus an extra conclusion that both bipartition sides have maximum degree > 2.
The conjecture is formalized faithfully and then negated.
The compactness counterexample is absent from the file.

flags.explanation: The failure-of-compactness result (the first main theorem) is not formalized.

The extra conjunct says every 2-coloring has both sides containing a vertex of degree > 2. This is not in the Theorem 1.2 statement and only strengthens it (it rules out the known Füredi/AKS case). Finset.sup over an empty side would be 0, so the conjunct also forces both sides to be nonempty.
